text: I need to understand the nature of this altered mentation: have you experienced any seizures, confusion, or hallucinations, and have you had any recent head trauma or contact with tick-infested areas?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that history. Given your fever and altered mental status, have you noticed any specific skin rash, joint pain, or muscle aches? Also, have you traveled to any rural areas recently or spent time outdoors where ticks might be present?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS) secondary to Haloperidol use, likely triggered by recent fever or dehydration; the clinical triad of fever, altered mentation, and generalized rigidity in a patient on antipsychotics is diagnostic. Immediate discontinuation of haloperidol and initiation of supportive care with dantrolene or bromocriptine are indicated.
